info.title: Predictive Trading Lab API
info.summary: Read-only gateway over the Predictive Trading Lab C++ engine.
info.description:
The engine is the single source of truth. This layer serializes what the engine computes and never recomputes it.

**Read-only.** Every endpoint is a GET and nothing mutates engine state.

**Two kinds of endpoint.** Capability endpoints report what the engine can do. Artifact endpoints serve what a session previously wrote -- and answer `available: false` when nothing has, rather than returning an empty portfolio that would render as a real book worth nothing.

get.description: Deliberately does not use the engine dependency: that would turn an unreachable engine into a 503 on the health endpoint itself, which is the one endpoint that must still answer when things are broken.
The same values `ptl_version` prints. A client can show whether the running engine reproduces the v1.0 reference build.

get.summary: Health, version and fingerprints in one call
get.description: Aggregated so a client renders a status bar with one request rather than three. Fingerprints are omitted rather than faked when the configuration cannot be read.

get.summary: Configuration hash for a config file
get.description: Returns the hash the engine computes, not the file contents. The gateway does not parse TOML: doing so would be a second reader that could disagree with the engine's.
The nine optimizers the engine registers, and what each requires. Running one needs a covariance matrix in a request body and is not part of the read-only surface.
What the engine computes. Producing a series requires a return history in a request body and is not part of the read-only surface.

Live risk state -- current exposure and utilisation -- requires a running session and is not available in the read-only surface. Serving a zeroed risk panel would show an account with no exposure, which is indistinguishable from a flat book.

get.summary: Account state from the last persisted session snapshot
get.description: Sourced from what a session wrote, not from a live book. `available: false` when no session has run.

get.summary: Open positions from the last persisted session snapshot
Operational metrics from a persisted snapshot
get.description: The engine's ops metrics live in the process that ran the session. The gateway serves the last snapshot written to disk; it does not report its own request counts, which would be gateway telemetry presented as engine state.
404 when the report does not exist. Unlike portfolio state, a report requested by id is a specific thing the caller believes exists, so absence is an error rather than a normal empty state.
Served from the snapshot the driver published, so reading never touches the session and costs the trading loop nothing.

post.description:
Refused with 409 if a session is already running: starting a second would abandon the first one's book without closing it out.

Market data is a **deterministic synthetic replay**. ADR-0001's entitlement is unverified and no live feed exists, so a given seed always produces the same session.

409.description: The current lifecycle state does not permit this.

post.description: Runs the engine's close-out: on_stop, trade matching and journal reconciliation, the same sequence a backtest performs.

409.description: The current lifecycle state does not permit this.

post.summary: Stop the session and start a new one
post.description: Explicitly **not** an in-place reset. Discarding a book where it stands would skip the close-out that reconciles the journal, so this is a stop followed by a start with the same guarantees as performing them separately.

409.description: The current lifecycle state does not permit this.

get.summary: Account, positions, orders and fills in one consistent read
get.description: A single document, so a dashboard renders one instant. Assembling it from four calls would let the account and the positions come from different moments.

Served from the snapshot the driver published. The host samples the portfolio on the driver thread; a reader fetching history on demand would have to call into the session from a request thread and break the single-writer guarantee.

Drawdown comes from the engine's own tracker. The gateway computes nothing.
Id to symbol. Only what the session actually trades: listing a wider universe would imply positions it cannot hold.

post.description:
Pure computation: the same request always produces the same response, and no session state is touched.

An optimizer that cannot answer raises rather than returning zeros — a silently flat weight vector looks like a deliberate decision to hold nothing.

422.description: The engine refused, and says why.

post.summary: Estimate a covariance and correlation matrix
post.description: Diagnostics travel with the matrix. When the estimator substitutes a simpler model — too few observations for the asset count — it says so, so a caller cannot use a degraded estimate believing it is a full one.

422.description: The engine refused, and says why.

post.summary: Rolling volatility, Sharpe, VaR and CVaR
post.description: Values before the window fills are `null`, never zero. A zero would draw a line through the origin that no data supports.

422.description: The engine refused, and says why.

post.summary: Split returns into beta and alpha contributions
post.description: A mismatched benchmark is refused rather than truncated: pairing each return with the wrong observation produces a beta that means nothing.

422.description: The engine refused, and says why.

post.summary: Semantic validation of a risk limit set
post.description:
Catches values that parse perfectly and are still wrong: a limit of zero rejects every order, and a limit of 1e9 can never bind while reading as protection on a control report.

Every issue is reported at once — an operator fixing a config should get one list, not six consecutive failed starts.

AccountSummary.title: AccountSummary
AccountSummary.description:
The account fields a persisted session snapshot carries.

Every field is optional: a snapshot written by an older session may not
carry all of them, and inventing a zero would be worse than omitting it.

ArtifactEnvelope.title: ArtifactEnvelope
ArtifactEnvelope.description:
A persisted artifact, or an explicit statement that none exists.

`available: false` is a normal answer, not an error. No session runs inside
the gateway, so this data exists only if a session previously wrote it.

examples.detail: no session state has been persisted at 'paper/never_ran/state'

keys.title: Keys
keys.description: Sorted, so two calls agree. Directory order is filesystem-defined.

observations.title: Observations
observations.description: Rows are observations, columns are assets. All rows equal length.

shrinkage.title: Shrinkage
shrinkage.description: Negative selects the engine's automatic intensity.

min_observations_ratio.title: Min Observations Ratio
min_observations_ratio.description: Observations per asset required before a full matrix is estimated. Lowering it disables a guard the engine applies deliberately.

degradation_reason.title: Degradation Reason
degradation_reason.description: Populated when the estimator substituted a simpler model. A caller must not use a degraded estimate without knowing it was degraded.

EngineSessionState.title: EngineSessionState
EngineSessionState.description:
The host's own view. Every field optional: before the first start there
is no session to describe, and inventing zeros would show a book that does
not exist.

stride.title: Stride
stride.description: Points were downsampled by taking every nth. Stride rather than averaging: averaging smooths away the drawdown troughs a reader is looking for.

EquityHistory.title: EquityHistory
EquityHistory.description:
Sampled equity history and drawdown.

Sampled by the session host on the driver thread and published with the
snapshot, so reading it never touches the session. Drawdown comes from the
engine's own tracker -- the gateway computes nothing.

ErrorDetail.title: ErrorDetail
ErrorDetail.description:
The shape of every error body.

`detail` carries the ENGINE's own message where there is one. An optimizer
that refuses says why, and that reason is more useful than anything the
gateway could invent.

examples.detail: minimum variance needs a covariance matrix

matches_reference.title: Matches Reference
matches_reference.description: False means this engine does not reproduce the v1.0 reference build, which is worth knowing before trusting a backtest from it.

status.title: Status
status.description: `unavailable` means the engine could not be reached at all.

examples.detail: the ptl bindings are not importable

examples.note: Running an optimization requires a request body and arrives in a later phase.

optimizer.title: Optimizer
optimizer.description: One of the names from GET /optimization.

covariance.title: Covariance
covariance.description: Square matrix. Required by minimum_variance; others degrade gracefully.

symbols.title: Symbols
symbols.description: Echoed back alongside the weights, for labelling.

binding_constraints.title: Binding Constraints
binding_constraints.description: Constraints that bound the solution. A weight sitting exactly on a limit is a constrained answer, not a free one, and the difference matters when reading the result.

requires_covariance.title: Requires Covariance
requires_covariance.description: The optimizer refuses without a risk model.

requires_expected_returns.title: Requires Expected Returns
requires_expected_returns.description: The optimizer refuses without forecasts. A zero forecast is a real opinion, not an absence of one, so none is assumed.

symbol.title: Symbol
symbol.description: Resolved by the host. An id alone leaks an internal index at the user.

validated_limits.title: Validated Limits
validated_limits.description: Limit fields the engine validates semantically.

require_live.title: Require Live
require_live.description: Live sessions require limits a backtest may legitimately omit.

available.title: Available
available.description: False before a session has started. Not an empty portfolio.

fills.title: Fills
fills.description: Most recent first, bounded to the last 200.

history.description: Equity series and drawdown, sampled by the host.

SessionSnapshot.title: SessionSnapshot
SessionSnapshot.description: One consistent read of the session.

replay_exhausted.title: Replay Exhausted
replay_exhausted.description: The replay ran out of events. Not an error and not a stop: the book stays readable, as a live session between market events.

seed.title: Seed
seed.description: Zero is rejected: a run whose seed is unknown cannot be reproduced.

StartRequest.title: StartRequest
StartRequest.description:
Parameters for a new paper session.

`seed` makes the run reproducible: the same seed replays the same synthetic
session, so a result can be reproduced rather than merely described.

fingerprints.description: Absent when the configuration could not be read.

SystemInfo.title: SystemInfo
SystemInfo.description:
Everything a status header needs, in one call.

Aggregated so a client does not fan out three requests to render one bar.

remedy.title: Remedy
remedy.description: What a correct value looks like.

ok.title: Ok
ok.description: False when any issue is fatal.

issues.title: Issues
issues.description: Every issue, not just the first: an operator should get one list.

transport.title: Transport
transport.description: Where the engine runs. Declared rather than inferred so a client can show it without guessing.

tags.name: compute
tags.description: Stateless computation: optimization, covariance, analytics, risk validation. POST because the inputs are matrices, not because anything is mutated.

tags.name: session
tags.description: Paper session lifecycle. The only endpoints that change anything, and they do so by enqueuing a command rather than touching the session.
